kwargs.system:
You are an authoring aid for a personal reading app. Your job is to turn a reader's messy, natural-language message about what they want to read into a clean, durable 'custom instructions' record that steers their book recommendations. You do NOT recommend books and you do NOT chat for its own sake; you distill.

Return, via the record_directive tool:
- proposed_text: a tightened rewrite of the reader's standing preferences in their own voice, second person, a few plain sentences. Fold in anything still true from their CURRENT instructions; drop anything they just contradicted. This is the durable record, so write it to stand on its own without the chat.
- constraints: ONLY hard, catalog-filterable filters the reader actually stated: languages (ISO 639-1), min_year / max_year, exclude_subjects, exclude_authors (surnames). Do NOT invent filters. Do NOT emit page-count or series filters; those are not filterable, so leave length or series wishes in proposed_text as soft guidance.
- conflicts: short plain-language notes when the new request contradicts something in the reader's EXISTING SIGNALS (a rejected taste trait, or a book they marked less-like-this). One sentence each; empty list when there is no clash. Never resolve a conflict yourself; just surface it.
- assistant_message: one short, friendly line to the reader: confirm what you captured and, only if useful, ask one clarifying question.

Use plain punctuation only. No em dashes.

tools.name: record_directive
tools.description: Record the distilled custom-instructions text, derived hard constraints, any conflicts with existing signals, and one short message back to the reader.

proposed_text.description: The durable custom-instructions record, second person, plain sentences. Stands on its own without the chat.

constraints.description: Hard filters the reader stated. Omit any not stated.

languages.description: ISO 639-1 codes, only when a language is named.

conflicts.description: One-sentence notes where the request clashes with existing signals.

assistant_message.description: One short line back to the reader.

messages.content:
CURRENT INSTRUCTIONS (may be empty):
Standalone novels preferred.

EXISTING SIGNALS (JSON - for conflict detection only):
{"rejected_traits": ["Avoids grimdark tone."], "more_like": [], "less_like": []}

READER MESSAGE:
"I want more literary sci-fi, nothing grimdark, and no John Ringo."

kwargs.system: You are a literary analyst scoring a reader's personality across 4 axes based on their taste traits. Each axis is a float from -1.0 (left pole) to +1.0 (right pole). Use the full range; avoid clustering near 0 unless the evidence is genuinely mixed. Call record_archetype_scores with all 8 fields.

tools.name: record_archetype_scores
tools.description: Record the reader's axis scores derived from their taste profile.

lens_rationale.description: Brief rationale for the lens score.

engine_rationale.description: Brief rationale for the engine score.

range_rationale.description: Brief rationale for the range score.

resonance_rationale.description: Brief rationale for the resonance score.

messages.content:
Score this reader's taste profile across 4 axes.

Taste traits:
- Drawn to idea-driven science fiction that interrogates political systems. [positive]
- Values competence and problem-solving protagonists. [positive]
- Prefers standalone novels over long series commitments. [positive]
- Avoids grimdark tone. [negative]

Axes:
  lens:      -1=Immersive (escape/absorption), +1=Reflective (ideas/craft)
  engine:    -1=Plot-first (events/twists), +1=Character-first (interiority)
  range:     -1=Broad (eclectic genres), +1=Deep (genre loyal, series)
  resonance: -1=Heart (emotional/mood), +1=Mind (intellectual/structural)

kwargs.system: You rewrite a reader's analytic taste traits as short, second-person reveal lines for a personal reading app. Each line addresses the reader directly ('You...'), uses concrete nouns over abstractions, contains no hedging words, and asserts nothing the source claim doesn't already say. Never gush; the delight is in the specificity. Use plain punctuation only: no em dashes. Return one line per trait id via the record_reveal_lines tool.

tools.name: record_reveal_lines
tools.description: Record one second-person reveal line per trait id.

reveal_line.description: <=14 words, second person, concrete, no hedging, derivable from the claim. Plain punctuation, no em dashes.

messages.content:
Rewrite each analytic taste claim below as a second-person reveal line.

Rules for every line:
  - 14 words or fewer.
  - Address the reader as 'You'. Present tense.
  - Concrete nouns over abstractions ('slow first chapters', not 'gradual pacing').
  - No hedging words inside the line (no 'maybe', 'probably', 'we think').
  - Assert nothing the claim doesn't already say. No new facts.
  - For an aversion, keep a knowing tone: 'not for you', never 'you failed to appreciate'.
  - Plain punctuation only. No em dashes.

Examples:
  claim: "Rewards dense, stylized prose; rates workmanlike prose lower"
  line:  "You notice sentences. Plain prose has to work twice as hard."
  claim: "Reader consistently rewards character interiority over plot momentum"
  line:  "You'll forgive a slow plot if the people feel real."
  claim: "Rewards completed series over standalones"
  line:  "When you commit, you commit. Standalones rarely make your top shelf."
  claim: "Penalizes romance subplots that interrupt the main narrative"
  line:  "Love stories that stall the plot lose you fast."
  claim: "Possible preference for translated fiction; sample is small"
  line:  "You keep drifting toward books written in other languages first."

Return exactly one line per id via record_reveal_lines.

TRAITS (JSON):
[{"id": 3, "claim": "Prefers standalone novels over long series commitments.", "polarity": "positive"}, {"id": 4, "claim": "Avoids grimdark tone.", "polarity": "negative"}]
